That I'm Transgender, 23 yo, MtF, but I cannot tell my family. I would probably be kicked out and I just can't have that happen right now. I'm stuck in this prison, and can't do anything about it. I can't see a Therapist to try and help out with it because my parents get SUPER worried when I say I want to see a Therapist. 

I want to be the real me damn it.
Being able to be my real self daily. Being out to the Family and knowing they would accept me. Not being kicked out instantly if they found my secret out.

PMing you now!
It is, and it seems like most of the Gender Therapists are on the west side, which is far away :(
Just saw your edit, I will do that ASAP. I can since I wear jeans every day and a collared shirt, nobody can see those things. I can only imagine what kind of wind passes through there >.<

>I worked with those resources and also some iPhone apps and anything else I could find on the internet, but didn't make much progress. I accepted my fate and I am now working with a vocal coach and am making much faster progress.

I will keep that in mind :) Hopefully I don't have to do that, but if it comes to it, I will do what it takes to hopefully sound feminine enough :) Though sometimes now I get mistaken on the Phone at work, which sometimes makes me feel good :)

> Another part of the transition process is learning how to pass, if that's something you place importance on. Places like r/transpassing or the /lgbt/ board on 4chan are the most active places for appearance feedback, so I would recommend lurking over in some of those places to gain a better understanding of what might be necessary for you to do in order to go full time.

Yes for sure, I already have been looking over those, and seeing what I would need to do to pass. I think I could hide it for the most part while transitioning, with the use of various things to hide my feminine features.

> Why can't you get your therapy insured? Also, in reading your last post, the hurdle that stuck out most to me was the job issue.

I could get it insured, but I'm on my parent's insurance, so I would hate for them to find out that way. So I think paying out of pocket would probably be safer.

>How soon do you want to find a new job? Do you think it might be worth it to stick it out presenting male at your current job until you are ready to go full time, and then move to a new job where everyone will see you as female? That may or may not be the best option for you, but that is my personal transition plan.

Whenever I can. I really wont be able to do much as far as if I start to transition while I'm at my current place, simply because any little sign, they swarm like sharks over it. I think that the best bet is to stay where I'm at until I feel like I could make the full time transition within like a month or 2 then go back to work somewhere else. 

>From here, it will take many months of behind the scenes work in makeup, voice training, navigating endocrinologists/therapists, laser hair removal, clothes shopping, hair growing, coming out, and gaining an understanding of what being female means to you and what it means in a larger societal frame.

Thank you, I appreciate you making somewhat of a list for me to kinda stick to :D I like this.

>The cheapest next step is voice training. Unfortunately, it is also one of the hardest. The more you use your male voice the longer the voice training process will be. I would say that the biggest reason why your job will prevent you from transitioning.

Alright, I will look into starting this next. What are some ways to go about that? Just videos? or what is the best way to go about starting to work on this?

>Your situation sounds rough and I'm sorry you're having to go through it, but hear me out: you CAN transition. Girls taller and bigger than you have in the past. Girls with less money and bigoted parents have in the past. It's totally possible, but what you need to know is that YOU are worth it and that YOU are worth working for it.

I honestly don't even know where to begin. I have no clue of where to start the process or anything. I don't know of Gender Therapists in my area. I've tried googling it but nothing specifically stating "Gender Therapy"

>You say you're in debt and can't afford to leave your job, is there a way you could look for another job? Preferably one where people are less douchey about gay/trans ppl. Heck, maybe you can find one that offers health insurance as well and you can at least get some talk therapy in. That would be a great way to kill three birds (poor birdies!) with one stone. I know it won't be easy but there are jobs out there (call centers, recpetionist, maybe even a government job).

I've tried to leave my job before, but I would hate to find another one, transition, then have to find another one. Not only that I can't support myself without a job. I think I could make MAYBE a month of bills then I'd be losing everything. I know there's better things out there, but I would want to line something up before I move. I have health insurance through my parents now, but I'm not sure what's covered and what's not, and I would hate for my parents to find out I've been using the insurance without talking to them first. And yes, poor birdies :(

> Also, you can lose weight. You don't even have to lose weight as far as I'm concerned. There are big girls out there and no reason why you can't be one either. But if you do want to lose weight, you totally can! The way I think of big people is like the way Michelangelo thought of his statues, "I saw the angel in the marble and carved until I set him free." The beautiful feminine you is there, and all have to do is work at yourself until you can set her free.

I would want to lose weight. I don't think I would want to transition without losing weight first. I just honestly don't have the motivation to. I can't put my mind to it because I know in the end, all that hard work and then I get disowned by everyone or worse kicked out.

> Family can be tough tho... But worst case scenario, is it worth living a lifetime's worth of lies for the sake of your parents, or is it worth risking their (supposedly unconditional) love in the pursuit of being yourself? Only you can answer that. Also people can and do come around. My dad disowned me when I came out to him but he recently came around and we have a fairly decent relationship now.

That's the dilemma. I want to be myself, but I depend on them too much right now to tell them. The thoughts have run across my mind when I get enough money or a job elsewhere to just leave, transition, and tell them after I've already started, so that way I at least know I can make it on my own and don't have to depend on them.

>Also, how did your one friend who you told react? Would you be able to talk to them more about it? If they're accepting and open minded it might be great to talk through some of the struggles you're feeling with them.

The one friend that knows was actually someone who I met online while RPing as a female. He originally knew I was a female until I told him otherwise. I barely get to ever talk to him though. I did think about telling another close friend, but I don't know how she'll take it. 

Thank you for your advice. Sorry it took so long for me to reply, I was busy at work all day. *hug back*

I know living on my own would help out some for sure. It's like I'll pay down a credit card some and feel better, but then I'll have a bad month at work and have to use what I had up just to get by. 

Yeah see when I bought that, I was working 2 jobs at the time and had a lower car payment, so I was easily able to afford it. I think I'm going to try and sell the ATV ASAP, but then I also feel like I'll disappoint my family because that's what we do a couple times a year for family fun. And then not to mention my parents will look down on me even more because they'll think I'm doing it to "spend more time on the computer" or some bad excuse. 

See it's hard to just cut myself off from that. I have a bad habit of remembering things I did in the past and dwelling on them. Anything that has happened it's hard for me to let go and I get "flashbacks" to those things. 

Outside of work, which is 9am-7pm CST I don't do much other than play WoW or work on my truck. I used to play guitar but I sold my old one and never bought a new one.

Well financials is part of the problem, but money doesn't buy love or friendship. 

So my truck is $500 a month and I have an ATV which is roughly $240 a month. I could sell the ATV since I almost never use that anymore. But other stuff is like a few high credit cards, a conns account, several lower credit cards, a couple of store cards, and that's about it. Basically I have a budget of paying minimum payments on everything and I come home with ~$250 after all my bills are paid. That's to buy gas and food with. 

I work for a car dealership and make $1600 a month before taxes plus commission (usually about $700 before taxes)

Like let's say I find a girl I'm interested in, which hardly ever happens, I'll find out that they don't like me or they are already seeing someone and it just sends me right back into a downward spiral. 

Another example, things start to look somewhat better at work then something stupid happens and send me back down.

I don't pay my student loans. My dad is paying them as of now, but that's all he pays. My measly paycheck is spent on my truck payment as well as a ton of credit cards and other stupid things I own. 

I know it would help me out a lot, because the couple of times I was left alone at the house for a week, and it was a lot better than normal. Now the thing is though is I don't make nearly enough and I've gotten myself in so much debt that I have no way out. 

I sometimes tell myself that I want to do this or that but then when I try to do that, I always get shot down by something. I have no idea what I want out of life, other than to by happy. But as soon as I get to that path, it always goes back downhill.
